subject: general
question: Which of the following are produced in a neutralisation reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Salt and Water__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neutralisation Reaction ** it is a chemical reaction between acid and a base, resulting in a salt and water. Example **NaCl+ H₂O→ Na⁺ Cl⁻+ H₂O**

**Some Reaction formulas __**

__
 
• Acid and water reaction : HCl + H₂O → H₃O+ Cl-
 
• Precipitate and base Reaction : Ba(NO₃)₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄ ↓ + 2NaNO₃
 
• Salt and water reaction : NaCl + H₂O → Na⁺ Cl⁻ + H₂O
 
• Salt and acid: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combination** (**Synthesis**) **Reaction: **Two or more substances combine to form a new compound. Example: A + B → AB (e.g., 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O)
 
• **Decomposition** **Reaction**: A compound breaks down into simpler substances. Example: AB → A + B (e.g., 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O2)
 
• **Single** **Replacement** (**Displacement**) **Reaction:** One element replaces another in a compound. Example: A + BC → AC + B (e.g., Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂+ H₂)
 
• **Double** **Replacement** (**Displacement**) **Reaction: **Exchange of ions between two compounds. Example: AB + CD → AD + BC (e.g., AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃)
 
• **Combustion** **Reaction**: Rapid reaction of a substance with oxygen, often producing heat and light.Example: CxHy + O₂ → CO₂+ H₂O (e.g., CH₄+ 2O₂ → CO₂+ 2H₂O)
 
• **Redox** (**Oxidation**-**Reduction**) **Reaction**:- Definition: Involves the transfer of electrons between reactants. - Example: Zn + CuSO₄→ ZnSO₄ + Cu (oxidation: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e-, reduction: Cu²⁺ + 2e- → Cu)
 
• **Acid**-**Base** (**Neutralization**) **Reaction**: Definition: Reaction between an acid and a base to form water and a salt. Example HCl + NaOH → H₂O + NaCl
